newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Israeli minister says gets EU agreement on PLO HQ.
newsitem.headline: Israeli minister says gets EU agreement on PLO HQ.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said on Friday that the European Union Presidency had agreed not to send any delegations to visit the PLO's offices in East Jerusalem.
After two days of talks in Ireland, which currently holds the rotating EU presidency, Levy said he had briefed Irish ministers on the current state of the Middle East peace process.
He said Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) President Yasser Arafat had agreed to close its political offices in East Jerusalem, and the EU would respect this agreement.

"In my talks I understood that the EU had no intention to complicate things but rather to honour the agreements between the Palestinians and ourselves on this issue," he told reporters after a meeting with Irish Prime Minister John Bruton.
The PLO is based in the Gaza Strip self-rule enclave but has also met some visiting foreign delegations in its Orient House building in East Jerusalem.

Israel regards such foreign visits to Orient House as supporting PLO demands to make East Jerusalem the capital of a future Palestinian state. The city's fate is to be negotiated at final peace talks between the two sides.
Levy restated Israel's determination never to cede any part of the city. "We believe that Jerusalem is the unified capital of Israel and it should stay that way," he said.
Arafat said on Thursday that the issue of Jerusalem would either make or break Middle East peace and the city should become a capital for the Palestinians as well as the Israelis.

But Levy said it was too early to discuss such issues. "Arafat has a tendency from time to time to talk about issues that concern the final status in the future," he said. "We are busy with the implementation of the interim agreement which is already signed."
"As for the final status...we have sufficient time to address all these problems, probably to quarrel about them, and maybe to agree," Levy said.

EU foreign ministers are meeting in Tralee, southern Ireland, at the weekend, and Levy said Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring would brief them about the agreement between Israel and the PLO on Orient House.
"This message will be conveyed to the European ministers in order to clarify to them that there is a new situation and maybe a new assessment has to be made," Levy said.

The Middle East peace process will be one of the main items discussed at the informal meeting in Tralee. The EU is anxious that the current Israeli government show the same commitment to the peace process as its predecessors.
Levy said he did not expect any criticism of Israel to emerge from the meeting.

"I feel that there is a wish in Europe prevailing to see the (peace) process continuing and advancing," he said. "When both sides reach an agreement I think that friendly countries like the European countries would give their blessing to it."

Levy affirmed his government's commitment to the peace process. "Some people might call it a big and dangerous gamble ...but we will do everything possible on our side to see it will succeed, with courage and caution," he said.
After his talks with Bruton, Levy was due to travel to London to continue his five-nation European tour.
